activities.anchor: hold the trachea open like a hosepipe
activities.caption: pair each part of the airway with its job
activities.name: gxScaffoldMatch

config.prompt: The plumbing defends the factory — pair each part with its role:

pairs.right: hold the trachea open — without them every breath would collapse the airway
secrete the mucus that traps pathogens and particles
sweep the mucus-laden debris upward to be swallowed
the only place exchange happens — 300 million terminals

config.why: Everything above the alveolar endings is scaffolding — trachea, bronchi, bronchioles are the branching tree that serves the exchange surface.

config.text: At rest you breathe about %%0%% times a minute with a tidal volume near %%1%% mL. Inhalation is always %%2%% — muscles must contract to enlarge the chest — but exhalation at rest is %%3%%: the diaphragm relaxes and the elastic lung tissue recoils like a released balloon.
config.hint: Only during exercise do the internal intercostals actively force air out.

activities.anchor: breathe through a straw into a flask of limewater
activities.caption: inspired vs expired — drag across the breath
activities.name: gxInspiredCompare

config.prompt: The air you breathe out is not the air you breathed in — drag the divider:

before.label: inspired
before.text: About 21% oxygen, 0.04% carbon dioxide, variable water vapour, ~78% nitrogen.

after.label: expired
after.text: 16% oxygen — only a quarter extracted; 4% CO₂, a hundredfold rise; saturated with water vapour; nitrogen unchanged.

config.why: The limewater clouds within seconds; a cold mirror fogs because expired air is saturated. Rescue breathing runs on the 16% residue.

activities.anchor: The small oxygen extraction is worth pausing on
activities.caption: true or false — the buffer in the breath
activities.name: gxExtractionJudge

statements.s: Alveolar gas stays around 14–16% oxygen even at rest — a reservoir keeping the diffusion gradient strong between breaths.
statements.why: Because each breath only removes a quarter of the oxygen.

statements.s: Expired-air resuscitation (rescue breathing) works because expired air still contains about 16% oxygen.
statements.why: Enough to keep a casualty's blood oxygenated.

statements.s: Each breath extracts nearly all the oxygen it carries.
statements.why: Only about a quarter — expired air is not 'used up'.

statements.s: A sudden drop in exhaled CO₂ under anaesthesia signals a crisis before other instruments notice.
statements.why: The limewater test scaled up — the same chemistry read in real time in every operating theatre.

activities.anchor: diffuses into blood arriving at about 5 kPa
activities.caption: pin the venous O₂ pressure on the kPa scale
activities.name: gxVenousPlace

config.prompt: In the alveolus, oxygen sits at roughly 13–14 kPa. Venous blood arriving from the tissues — after they have taken their share — sits at about what partial pressure (kPa)?
config.why: About 5 kPa — the difference is the diffusion gradient; at 5,500 m altitude the whole hill shrinks to under 10 kPa, which is why mountaineers hyperventilate.
config.context: Haemoglobin multiplies the blood's oxygen capacity roughly 70-fold over what could dissolve in plasma alone.

config.prompt: From nose to alveolus, almost nothing gets through — put the defence in order:
items: The nose: hairs and turbinates warm, humidify and strain the air
Goblet cells secrete a sticky mucus carpet that traps anything larger than a few micrometres
Cilia beat the mucus upward at about 1–2 cm per minute
The entire mucus lining is swallowed reflexively many times an hour
Alveolar macrophages patrol and engulf whatever slips through
config.why: Smoke defeats all of it at once — paralysing cilia for hours and loading the mucus with tar; emphysema then literally dissolves alveolar walls, and lost surface area cannot be rebuilt.

activities.caption: call the magnitude — the sprinting bellows
activities.name: gxVentilationEstimate

config.prompt: Ventilation is about 6 L/min at rest. At maximum effort it can rise twenty-fold — roughly how many litres per minute?
config.why: About 120 L/min — while oxygen uptake rises only about fifteen-fold; at maximum effort ventilation tracks the CO₂ load almost perfectly.
config.context: You never decide to breathe harder during a sprint; the CO₂ decides for you — the brain is running a pH meter.

activities.caption: file the diseases by the Fick term they attack
activities.name: gxFickBuckets

config.prompt: Fick's law: rate ∝ area × difference ÷ thickness. File each disease by the term it removes:

items.label: emphysema merges hundreds of sacs into a few large ones
pulmonary fibrosis scars and thickens the membrane
pulmonary embolism cuts the blood supply
pure-O₂ therapy raising the difference term five-fold

config.why: Every feature of the alveolus is a term in Fick's equation — and clinical oxygen therapy is the one entry that works FOR the patient, steepening every gradient.
